draft.briefing: Hey, you're in T. Nagar! All these crowded shopping streets sit on what used to be the Long Tank, a huge reservoir west of old Madras that was drained in the 1920s to build a planned neighbourhood. Today it's one of the busiest shopping districts of its kind in Asia.
draft.hungryLine: Chennai's classic move is a plain vegetarian place for tiffin or a full meals plate, and around here you'll find plenty of them between the shops.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Ranganathan Street is a 5 min walk, and Panagal Park, the heart of the shopping district, is about 7 minutes away. Keep going and Pondy Bazaar is around 15 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Natesan Park on Venkatanarayana Road is an 8 min walk, a leafy 4 acre park where locals do their morning walks under neem, gulmohar and mahogany trees.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Pondy Bazaar's official name is actually Soundarapandianar Angadi, and T. Nagar itself was historically called East Mambalam.

spots.name: Ranganathan Street
spots.detail: 5 min walk · Often called the most crowded street in Chennai, packed with clothes and jewellery shops

status.text: Be ready to elbow your way through

spots.name: Panagal Park

spots.detail: 9 min walk · Venkateswara and Alamelu Manga temple at the TTD Information Center

tips.title: Bargain with a smile.
tips.body: Pondy Bazaar and Ranganathan Street are the places to try your bargaining skills on knick-knacks, just expect serious crowds.

tips.title: Come between November and February.
tips.body: Chennai is extremely hot and humid, especially in May, and those cooler months dodge the worst of the heat.

story.title: The Long Tank
story.body: This whole area was once covered by the Long Tank, a vast reservoir west of Madras city. It was part of the zamindari of Mambalam.

story.title: An old Shiva temple
story.body: The Kasi Viswanatha Temple in nearby West Mambalam was built in the 17th century. It's named after the Vishwanatha Temple at Varanasi.

story.title: A planned town
story.body: The Raja of Panagal's government drew up the Mambalam Town Planning Scheme to drain the Long Tank and build a planned neighbourhood. Panagal Park and the radial streets named after city officials and politicians date from then.

story.title: A park opens
story.body: Natesan Park opened to the public on 13 September 1950. It's still the only Chennai Corporation park with a separate tennis court for coaching kids.

story.title: Shopping central
story.body: Ranganathan Street, Usman Road and Pondy Bazaar are lined with jewellery, clothes, utensils and toy shops. Mambalam railway station next door handles around 200,000 passengers a day.
